Magnetic Level Switch Contact States at a Glance

A magnetic level switch gives an ON/OFF signal when the magnet inside the float moves next to the sealed reed switch in the stem. The float and the reed never touch, so the contact state depends only on where the liquid surface is. The table shows how a normally open (NO) and a normally closed (NC) reed behave as the level moves.

Float positionNO reed contactNC reed contactTypical use of the signal
Below the switch point, magnet away from reedOpenClosedNo action, or low level alarm when wired for low level
At the switch point, magnet beside reedClosedOpenHigh level alarm, pump stop or valve close
Falls back below the switch pointOpens againCloses againPump start or refill command
Float stuck or liquid foamingNo changeNo changeNeeds a periodic function test

How to check a magnetic level switch on site:

  1. Isolate the alarm or pump circuit so a test does not start equipment.
  2. Connect a multimeter in continuity mode across the reed terminals.
  3. Lift or lower the float by hand, or raise the tank level, past the switch point.
  4. Confirm the contact changes state exactly once and returns when the float moves back.
  5. Restore wiring and confirm the alarm or pump responds in the control panel.
